title: Making the neural plate

objective.text: Explain how signals from the midline decide what ectoderm becomes.

body.general: How does a plain sheet of cells decide to become the nervous system? The notochord, a rod of cells along the midline, signals the ectoderm, the top cell layer, above it [f1]. That ectoderm thickens into the neural plate, the start of brain and spinal cord [f1]. Ectoderm left alone tends to become neural tissue [f2]. A signal called BMP4 pushes it toward skin instead [f2]. The midline tissues release blockers of BMP4, so the ectoderm over them goes neural [f3]. Making one tissue change another like this is called induction [f1].
body.mbbs: The notochord and prechordal mesoderm induce the overlying ectoderm to thicken into the neural plate [f1]. Its cells are neuroectoderm [f7]. Ectoderm's default fate is neural; BMP4 diverts it to epidermis [f2]. The primitive node, notochord and prechordal mesoderm secrete noggin, chordin and follistatin [f3]. These bind and block BMP4, so midline ectoderm becomes neural plate [f3]. The blockers alone induce only forebrain and midbrain tissue [f4]. Hindbrain and spinal cord need WNT3a and FGF as well [f4]. Retinoic acid helps set head-to-tail identity along the plate [f5].

facts.text: The notochord and prechordal mesoderm signal the ectoderm above them to thicken into the neural plate, which forms the brain and spinal cord.
The neural plate's cells are called neuroectoderm.
Ectoderm left alone becomes neural tissue; the signal BMP4 turns it into epidermis (skin) instead.
The node, notochord and prechordal mesoderm release noggin, chordin and follistatin, which block BMP4, so the midline ectoderm goes neural.
Blocking BMP alone makes only forebrain and midbrain tissue; hindbrain and spinal cord also need WNT3a and FGF.
Retinoic acid helps set head-to-tail identity in the neural plate.
Ectoderm builds more than skin: it also makes the whole nervous system, the sense epithelia, the pituitary and tooth enamel.

misconceptions.right: Ectoderm also makes the whole nervous system, sense epithelia, pituitary and tooth enamel; the neural plate is ectoderm.

checks.prompt: Ectoderm lying over the notochord becomes which tissue?
checks.why: Ectoderm over the notochord thickens into the neural plate; ectoderm elsewhere becomes skin.

checks.prompt: What does BMP4 do to ectoderm when nothing blocks it?
checks.why: Ectoderm's own default is neural; BMP4 pushes it toward skin.

checks.prompt: How do the midline signals noggin and chordin make midline ectoderm neural?
options: They add a neural signal on top of BMP4
They move cells into the midline
checks.why: They bind and block BMP4, so the ectoderm keeps its default neural fate.

adult: The neural plate goes on to build the brain and spinal cord [f1].

remember.q: Which tissues induce the neural plate?
remember.a: The notochord and prechordal mesoderm, signalling the ectoderm above them [f1].

remember.q: What does BMP4 do to ectoderm?
remember.a: Turns it into epidermis; without BMP4, ectoderm becomes neural [f2].

remember.q: What extra signals do hindbrain and spinal cord need?
remember.a: WNT3a and FGF, beyond the BMP blockers [f4].
